text:
Jack St. Ivany needed 2 minutes and 21 seconds to get his first NHL goal, and he got it on a shot our model gave less than a 1% chance. A defenseman the Flyers took 112th overall in 2018, who once went a full AHL season in Wilkes-Barre without scoring, beat Akira Schmid with a snap shot from nowhere. It was that kind of afternoon in Washington: strange, loud, and not decided by the people you'd expect.

Florida answered fast. Brady Tkachuk scored 52 seconds later off a feed from his brother Matthew, then scored again on the power play at 10:00, Matthew and Seth Jones assisting. In between, the game turned ugly: Tom Wilson was given a major for boarding and a game misconduct for a hit that sent Sandis Vilmanis out of the game, as ESPN reported. The Capitals finished with 23 penalty minutes to Florida's 8 and spent a long stretch of the afternoon a forward short.

They won anyway, and they won it at even strength, where they out-chanced Florida 2.82 expected goals to 1.53. Alex Tuch, whose exit from Buffalo is still producing headlines, tied it at 4:39 of the second. At 14:55 Aliaksei Protas put Washington ahead, the swing of the game in our win model (52% to 74%), with Pierre-Luc Dubois and Ryan Leonard on the play. That trio has only been together since Tom Gulitti of NHL.com reported the line shuffle on Tuesday. Dubois made it 4-2 early in the third, the period Washington owned 2.02 to 1.16 in expected goals. Sam Bennett's deflection with 47 seconds left made the finish nervous and nothing more.

Logan Thompson, pulled earlier in the week, was steady (27 saves, a little better than expected). Schmid stopped Alex Ovechkin on a 38% look in the third, the best chance that didn't go in.

The Capitals deserved this one 55% of the time, which is about how it felt. For Florida, the bigger worry walked off in the first period.
headline: St. Ivany scores first, Capitals finish without Wilson
